truth: High Rock is a wet, broken country of sea bluffs, river meadows and moors, walled on the east by the Wrothgarian Mountains. The Bretons are a people of mixed Nedic and elven blood, shaped by the Direnni elves who ruled them first and split the land into dozens of petty kingdoms. The Warp in the West folded most of the bay's kingdoms into a few crowns, but every former king is now a baron with a keep, a banner and a grudge. Knights, guilds and covens fill the gaps that the law leaves, while the Orcs hold the mountains. Wool, hides, grain, ships and ore fund the crowns and merchant guilds.

daggerfall.truth: The crown's own country: sea bluffs, a river through the capital, sheep on the moors and fog in the coves. Daggerfall grew rich on hides, wool and the river toll, and it rules seven fiefs whose lords were kings before the Warp. The Glenpoint headland watches for smugglers and Sentinel's ships, because the old war over Betony was never settled. The Vraseth bloodline feeds quietly in the moor keeps. Witches live on the bluffs, and the court uses them while pretending not to.

anticlere.truth: River meadows under a long cliff line, the breadbasket of the western bay, with a dark wood to the north. Anticlere is pious and rich in grain, and its Knights of the Flame want to clear the haunted woods of Ykalon and Phrygias and settle them. Every settler party that goes north loses someone. Castle Llugwych sits in that wood, and the Skeffington coven sells safe passage. Orc bands from the old wars still hold strongholds in the Phrygias hills.

dwynnen.truth: A gorge-cut march between the two crowns, the smallest and hardest realm on the northern shore. Dwynnen city spans a deep limestone gorge with a single stone bridge that carries the North Shore Road. Its Order of the Raven fought on the losing side of the old petty wars and the realm still owes Wayrest's bankers for it. Disbanded soldiers turned bandit fill the Kambria crossroads, which is why Daggerfall's data gives Kambria nine prisons and eight bandit holds. Giants and harpies come down from the eastern hills toward Alcaire and Koegria.

wayrest.truth: The richest city on the bay, at the mouth of the Bjoulsae. Wayrest's merchant guilds own the ships, the quays and half the barons' debts; the crown owns the harbour chain and wants the rest. Out in the bay the Direnni Tower stands on Balfiera, older than any Breton crown. Inland, the Orsinium Area is a Breton fief round the ruins of a fallen Orc city, and Orsinium wants it back. A dead king of Daggerfall lies in Menevia, which is either an honour or a theft depending on who tells it.

wrothgar.truth: The mountain wall of High Rock: granite peaks, high cold valleys and the richest ore in the province. In the north the Orcs keep Orsinium on its plateau and live by Malacath's code in strongholds that each work a mine. In the south, Breton barons in Newing work the same ore with hired miners and call the valleys theirs. Orsinium has been sacked and rebuilt more than once, and every fall left a ruin and a grudge. The Daughters of Wroth keep a coven in the high woods. Dwemer halls run under the range.

glenumbra.truth: Glenumbra is the wettest, oldest country in High Rock: ocean cliffs on the western sea, wide heather moors over granite and peat, and mist-filled valleys climbing north from the Iliac crowns. Camlorn stands on a rocky hill above the moors as a walled cathedral city of gothic spires, famous for its bells, its weavers and its court. Out on the peat bogs the earth-witches of the Glenmoril Wyrd guard an ancient sacred grove against corruption, uneasy neighbours to Mara's cathedral priests. Cairns and barrows mark the First-Era battlefield where Bretons and Direnni broke the Alessian army, and restless dead stir whenever the sea fog rolls inland.

rivenspire.truth: Rivenspire is a cold, stern country of dark granite crags, narrow gorges and wind-scoured plateaus along the northern sea. Shornhelm sits in a mountain gap as a disciplined military city beneath a red stone keep, where three rival noble houses share watch duties and quarrel over the crown. On the northern cliffs, Northpoint guides timber and ore ships into harbour by its twin beacon lamps. Ravens nest on every tor, and the land feels older and bleaker than the bay shore: Nedic crag barrows crown the ridges, vampire-tainted bloodlines plot in stone manors, and the shattered spire of Doomcrag casts a shadow over the western hills.

stormhaven.truth: Stormhaven is the green woodland belt north of the Iliac crowns: rolling hills of oak and beech, clear streams and old stone highways linking Anticlere and Dwynnen to the Bjoulsae and Wayrest. It is Mara's heartland in High Rock, a country of wayside shrines, abbey farms and pilgrim inns where travellers stop on their way to the great cathedrals. Beneath that gentle surface, petty barons tax the pilgrim roads, Daedric revellers lure the unwary into hidden demesnes, and the Stone Giant weeps beside the highway while bandits and coven witches work the deep forest glens.

bjoulsae.truth: The Bjoulsae region follows High Rock's great eastern river from its highland lakes down through a steep valley between Wrothgar and the Druadach Mountains. Evermor stands on a lake island reached by a stone causeway, its cathedral and water-relic drawing pilgrims while its barges carry Wrothgar's ore and timber down to Wayrest. Across the eastern ridges lies Skyrim's Reach, so this is a marchland of watchtowers, border forts and horse ranches: Reachfolk raiders slip over the passes to burn river steads, and drowned crypts lie beneath the island foundations of the lake.
